video_title: The Next Trillion Dollar Crypto Opportunity with Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
gist: The head of Coinbase Asset Management argues crypto is mid-bear — Bitcoin around $64,000-$67,000 in late July 2026, roughly 50% below the November 2025 peak of $126,000 — with perpetual funding rates just turning positive as a bottoming signal after the October 2025 leverage wipeout. His forward thesis is that the next cycle belongs to onchain asset management: Bitcoin-collateral yield strategies, stablecoin-funded hybrid credit that arbitrages tokenized paper against its traditional version, and vault infrastructure that regulated managers are about to flood into. He also argues the fat protocol thesis is losing, with value accruing to licensed distribution platforms rather than tokens.

insights.claim: Bitcoin peaked at $126,000 in November 2025 and as of late July 2026 trades around $64,000-$67,000, roughly 50% below the cycle top.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Sets the reference frame for drawdown math: a ~50% decline from peak is in line with prior Bitcoin cycles rather than a structural break.
insights.quote: we absolutely peaked in November of last year 2025 126,000

insights.claim: The consensus 2025 call that Bitcoin's four-year cycle was dead and a five-year cycle was the new norm has been proven wrong by the current drawdown, meaning historical cycle periodicity still holds.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If periodicity holds, the timing of the bottom and the next expansion can be modeled off prior cycles rather than treated as unprecedented.
insights.quote: the four-ear cycle's dead, the 5year cycle is the new norm was the big call. I I think we can stand here today and look back and say absolutely that's a wrong call

insights.claim: The expected Bitcoin bottom ranges from an extreme low near $35,000 to a softer bottom in the high $40,000s to low $50,000s, and such lows typically print as sharp weekend wicks that recover five or six thousand points within a day, making them uncatchable.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete band for scaling in and argues for resting bids or programmatic accumulation over discretionary bottom-timing.
insights.quote: Um the market expects the price range to be anywhere from on the extreme low ends 35,000 to a more soft bottoming, you know, maybe in the low 50s or high high 40s.

insights.claim: Roughly $60-70 billion was raised in 2025 to fund digital asset treasury vehicles, with nearly all of it flowing into Bitcoin and creating insatiable buying demand that captured supply at the top of the cycle.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Identifies the marginal buyer that drove the 2025 top; with that fundraising channel closed, demand for the next leg has to come from a different source.

themes.theme: Leverage Flush and Funding Rates as Regime Signal

insights.claim: The October 10, 2025 liquidation event wiped out more than $25 billion across multiple non-US exchanges and was the single catalyst that started this bear market, analogous to FTX, Three Arrows, BlockFi and Celsius triggering the 2022 bear.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Frames the drawdown as a leverage-structure event rather than a demand collapse, which implies recovery tracks the rebuild of leverage, not new narratives.
insights.quote: The funding rate the leverage wipeout in October of 10 October of 2025 was the big catalyst that sent us into this bare market.

insights.claim: Perpetual funding rates were unattractive and at times deeply negative for the past six months but are now turning positive again, which is treated as an important bottoming signal showing capitulation is largely done and strong hands are re-levering.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: A free, daily-observable indicator for regime change; sustained positive perp funding is the tell that the market-neutral yield trade is coming back.

insights.claim: The Bitcoin funding rate arbitrage trade (long spot, short perpetual or future) returned roughly 4-8% net from 2021 through 2024 and spiked into the high teens or low 20s for weeks or months at a time, but is entirely leverage-driven and collapses in bear markets.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Benchmarks what a market-neutral crypto yield product must clear, and warns that quoted historical yields are regime-dependent, not steady-state.

insights.claim: The post-capitulation recovery period runs about two-plus years during which leverage builds consistently and persistently, making funding and basis a durable source of alpha over that window.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If correct, the deployment window into market-neutral crypto yield vehicles is opening now and lasts roughly through the next cycle expansion.

insights.claim: Large Bitcoin holders with very low cost basis face only three options for liquidity — sell and take the tax hit while losing the beta, borrow against the coins and accept a liability mismatch, or deploy the Bitcoin as collateral into income strategies — and the third is the fastest-growing demand.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Defines a large pool of idle never-sell Bitcoin as the raw material for the yield-product category; whoever wins distribution to it captures a recurring fee stream.
insights.quote: The mantra in Bitcoin is never sell, right?

insights.claim: A Bitcoin yield fund can generate BTC-denominated income through three collateral strategies: harvesting options volatility premia by selling delta-managed puts and calls on Deribit (now fully integrated into Coinbase and described as the world's largest options exchange), capturing the basis and funding-rate spread, and cash-and-carry where Bitcoin collateral funds dollar borrowing reinvested into short-duration and high-yield credit.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: A replicable blueprint of where 'Bitcoin yield' actually comes from — useful for underwriting any competitor product claiming BTC-denominated income.

insights.claim: A durable Bitcoin yield strategy must deliberately combine procyclical sources such as funding rates, which only pay in bull markets, with countercyclical ones so it can produce income through both regimes.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Single-source BTC yield products dependent on funding will print near-zero returns in bear phases; regime diversification is the screen for allocators.

insights.claim: Coinbase Asset Management launched a stablecoin credit strategy in April 2026 whose fund shares are tokenized with Superstate on Base, Solana and Ethereum mainnet, and which accepts subscriptions directly in stablecoins rather than requiring a bank wire.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Stablecoin-native subscription removes the banking on-ramp friction that keeps crypto-native capital out of regulated funds — a distribution unlock to watch for copycats.

insights.claim: The stablecoin credit portfolio is roughly 80% traditional off-chain structured credit — CLOs, trade finance, asset-backed securities and accounts receivable — and only 20% tokenized credit, with 90 to 100 day liquidity and hundreds of underlying names per line item to strip out idiosyncratic risk.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The 'onchain yield' in institutional stablecoin products is mostly conventional structured credit; underwrite it as credit risk, not crypto risk.

insights.claim: Crypto-native credit is entirely floating rate while the vast majority of traditional credit is fixed rate and longer duration, and traditional credit funds simply do not function on chain, leaving two parallel and still-unconnected markets.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The rate-structure mismatch is the specific reason tokenized credit has not scaled; whoever solves fixed-rate on-chain issuance unlocks the far larger pool.
insights.quote: Everything in crypto is floating rate.

insights.claim: The core alpha thesis in tokenized credit is arbitraging the tokenized version of an instrument against its traditional version — holding one, the other, or both — the same way one arbs futures or options against the underlying equity, which only a hybrid TradFi and crypto manager can currently run.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Points to a nascent, uncrowded basis trade between wrapper and underlying, comparable to early ETF NAV arbitrage and the 1980s high-yield build-out.

insights.claim: Tokenized credit issued through regulated broker-dealers and transfer agents carries very little genuine smart-contract risk because US issuers must keep an off-chain ledger and can simply reissue the asset; the real risk is looping leverage across DeFi venues where an unwind in one vault forces selling in another.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Reframes RWA underwriting away from code exploits toward leverage and forced-selling contagion, and creates a playbook of waiting for the unwind then buying the wrapper at a discount to the underlying.
insights.quote: I may choose to just wait for the unwind to happen in the onchain market and then go in and buy everything at a discount.

insights.claim: Crypto investor demand is barbelled — investors want either pure directional beta or fully market-neutral spread returns, with almost no appetite for the low-volatility multi-strategy and trend products that dominate traditional finance.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Product designers and allocators launching middle-of-the-curve crypto strategies are aiming at a market that does not yet exist.

themes.theme: Fat Protocol Thesis and Where Value Accrues

insights.claim: Value in crypto is accruing to distribution platforms that hold the licenses and the customer relationship rather than to protocols and their tokens, which implies the fat protocol thesis is going away.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Argues for owning regulated distribution and exchange equity over layer-one tokens as the way to express crypto adoption.

insights.claim: Protocols pay their customer acquisition cost in their own tokens, granting hundreds of millions of dollars of tokens created out of thin air to distribution platforms for priority access, which is the cheapest equity and lowest cost of capital financing available and returns nothing to the token.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Explains structurally why token holders are diluted by growth, and why the same mechanism lets any better-funded rival displace an incumbent.
insights.quote: So their the customer acquisition cost is actually paid for with tokens, right? that were created out of thin air based off of the initial value of the company raised

insights.claim: Protocols reliably grow TVL, usage, customers and assets into the tens of billions without ever demonstrating the point at which a consistent revenue stream returns to the protocol.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: TVL and usage metrics should be discounted heavily in token valuation until a revenue-capture mechanism is demonstrated.
insights.quote: where does the revenue switch turn on, right? How do you prevent yourself from getting displaced by the next competitor who has a better uh who has a new token that they've raised

insights.claim: The counterweight to protocol pessimism is that during this bear market a set of protocols that historically served only crypto natives are being integrated into fintechs and large brokerage houses serving hundreds of millions of customers.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Enterprise integration during a bear market is the surviving-protocol screen — those are the candidates positioned to monetize in the next cycle.

themes.theme: Onchain Asset Management, Vaults and Regulation

insights.claim: The next crypto cycle will be defined by onchain asset management and by resolving what it means to be a fiduciary for customers on chain.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The speaker's highest-conviction forward call and his single most-anticipated theme for 2027; positions vault infrastructure and regulated managers as the trade.
insights.quote: The next cycle is going to be defined by onchain asset management

insights.claim: Over the next few months large regulated asset managers with compliance infrastructure and licenses will keep entering onchain asset management — JPMorgan has already announced its own vault on Kinexys, Bitwise is active, Grayscale has announced onchain asset management, and Fidelity and others are expected to follow.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Names the specific near-term catalyst set for on-chain AUM growth and for the crypto-versus-TradFi custody and discretion fight that will accompany it.

insights.claim: Vault architecture is an orders-of-magnitude improvement over traditional fund administration, which is too slow for markets that now trade 24/7/365, and the entire asset management industry from BlackRock down accepts that vault infrastructure must become part of core investment management.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Frames incumbent fund administrators as the disrupted party and vault tooling as an infrastructure category with a forced-adoption tailwind.
insights.quote: Everyone recognizes in the asset management community from Black Rockck down that we need vault infrastructure. It has to be a part of the core investment management landscape.

insights.claim: A vault is fundamentally just a stack of composable token standards — the speaker cites 4626 and 7744 and credits Centrifuge as a pioneer in launching them — each compounding on the last to replicate real-time pricing, NAV and attribution that traditional finance does manually.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The standards layer, not any single vault brand, is where the durable network effect sits, and Centrifuge is named as the leader defining it.

insights.claim: The unresolved regulatory question is whether a vault curator writing smart-contract allocation logic is exercising investment discretion and therefore acting as a fiduciary; Hester Peirce's recent comments deliberately opened dialogue without taking a position, a treatment the industry never got under Gensler, and her term is expected to end by year-end.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The biggest legal overhang on DeFi vault economics, and the favorable-rulemaking window may close with the departure of its main advocate.

insights.claim: Even once the Clarity Act goes live it will take a very long time for firms to decide whether to issue tokenized versus traditional equity and whether to raise on-chain or through traditional capital markets, comparable to firms still working through Dodd-Frank integrations from 2009.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations for a legislation-driven catalyst trade — passage is not adoption, and the tokenization revenue ramp is a multi-year story.

insights.claim: Institutional investors are structurally forced to minimize cash because their only real mandate is to beat inflation, beat money supply growth and outpace their liabilities, and the majority fail at all three and end up underfunded.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The debasement-hurdle framing is the actual sales wedge for Bitcoin into pensions; it reframes BTC as a liability-matching tool rather than a speculative sleeve.
insights.quote: the number one thing is can you beat monetary debasement and can you pay off your liabilities

insights.claim: Bitcoin is the only asset other than gold that combines fixed supply, global access and an offset to monetary debasement, and it has now proven a better return than equity markets and other asset classes.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The specific comparative claim underpinning pension allocation pitches; the entire case rests on the fixed-supply plus liquid-global-access combination that only gold shares.

insights.claim: Private equity and venture, long treated as the best alternative for beating liabilities, are now oversaturated and likely face a decade or two of less than good performance.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If institutions accept this, allocation dollars leaving PE must land elsewhere — the implied beneficiaries in his argument are Bitcoin and passive cap-weighted equity.

insights.claim: It is a great time to buy Bitcoin but investors should be selective about altcoins and take only smaller allocations to the majors, because it remains unresolved which networks will win and how tokens respond after the Clarity Act.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: An explicit BTC-over-alts stance from an institutional manager at bear-market lows, with token regulatory reclassification as the key altcoin catalyst.
insights.quote: Uh it's a great time to buy Bitcoin. This is not financial advice, but it's a great time to buy Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Asked to pick the biggest story of 2027, the speaker chooses stablecoin credit over tokenized treasuries.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Suggests the next leg of real-world-asset growth moves up the risk curve from government paper into private credit — a directional bet on where tokenized AUM concentrates.

insights.claim: Privacy is the most underappreciated theme in crypto because institutions do not want the market to see their movements or ping their wallets, though the right expression may be privacy built into architecture rather than owning privacy coins.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Flags institutional transaction privacy as a prerequisite for large on-chain flows, and separates the infrastructure bet from the privacy-coin beta bet.
insights.quote: I think privacy is still vastly underappreciated and underfocused on.
